chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad and others, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Abu 'Ubayda who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about the menstruating woman who sees signs of purity while she is on a journey, and she does not have with her enough water for her ghusl, and the time for salat has come.
He said: 'If she has with her enough water to wash her private part, then she should wash it, then perform tayammum and pray.'
I said: 'Can her husband come to her (conjugally) in that state?' He said: 'Yes. If she has washed her private part and performed tayammum, there is no problem.'

key_terms.التيمم: Tayammum; dry ablution using clean earth/dust, substituting for wudu or ghusl when water is unavailable
key_terms.الحائض: The menstruating woman; one in the state of hayd (menstrual impurity)
key_terms.السفر: Travel/journey; a context that permits legal concessions (rukhsa) in Islamic law
key_terms.الطهر: Purity; the end of the menstrual period marked by the cessation of blood
key_terms.الغسل: Ghusl; the obligatory full ritual bath required after major ritual impurity
key_terms.لا بأس: There is no objection/harm; a jurisprudential formula indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: What should a menstruating woman traveling without enough water for ghusl do when prayer time arrives?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a legal ruling for a traveling woman who reaches purity from menstruation but lacks sufficient water for a full ghusl. She must wash her private part with the available water, then substitute the rest of the ghusl with tayammum, after which both salat and marital intimacy become permissible. This hadith illustrates the Islamic legal principle that necessity and hardship (especially in travel) allow for substituting water-based purification with dry ablution.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, and someone else, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the menstruating woman seeking the purity, and she is during the journey, and there is no water with her. What would suffice her for her washing, and the Salaat has presented itself?’
Heasws said: ‘When it was such that there was water with her of a measure with which she can wash her private part, so she should wash it. Then she would perform Tayammum and pray Salaat’.
I said, ‘So can her husband come to her during that state?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. When she has washed her private part and performed Tayammum, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Muhammad and others have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from abu ‘Ubaydah who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about the case of a woman who after Hayd (menses) experiences a Hayd-free condition during a journey and cannot find water enough for Ghusl (bath) when it is time for Salah (prayer).
He (the Imam) said, ‘If she has enough water to wash clean her private parts, she must do so and take Tayammum instead of Ghusl (bath); then perform Salah (prayer).
5 I then asked, ‘What happens if her husband comes? 5 He (the Imam) said, ‘After her washing clean her private parts and Tayammum it is not harmful.
